chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who said to another, 'Give me your sheep and camels, and they will be with me; when they give birth, I will replace them for you, if you wish, females with males or males with females.' He (AS) said, 'That is a disliked action, unless he replaces them after they are born and separates them.'

He said, 'And I asked him about a man who gives to another man cows and sheep on the condition that he returns to him every year a specific amount of their milk and offspring.' He (AS) said, 'All of that is disliked.'

key_terms.مَكْرُوهٌ: Disliked (a category of legal ruling less severe than forbidden)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging the gender of livestock offspring in a partnership contract according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarates the permissibility of livestock partnership (*mudarabah*) by distinguishing between acceptable and disliked (*makruh*) conditions. He specifically prohibits pre-determined exchanges of offspring gender or fixed quotas of milk and young, as these introduce *gharar* (uncertainty) regarding the specific assets being transferred. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on ensuring clarity in the subject matter of contracts to avoid disputes arising from ambiguous future outcomes.
